subsystems.name: Accelerator
subsystems.role: gives the payload its speed before release — either a spinning arm or a linear electromagnetic track.
parts: linear motor coils and stator track (electromagnetic type)

subsystems.name: Energy supply and pulsed drive
subsystems.role: delivers a large burst of energy in seconds or a steady spin-up over minutes.

subsystems.name: Vacuum and release system
subsystems.role: removes air drag, then lets the payload leave at the right instant.
parts: seal or membrane at the exit

subsystems.name: Payload carrier
subsystems.role: carries the payload through huge acceleration and, from Earth, through the lower atmosphere.

subsystems.name: Aiming and control
subsystems.role: points the release vector so the payload meets its target trajectory.

subsystems.name: Launch site
subsystems.role: the ground installation, sized around the machine and its safety exclusion zone.

buildSteps.title: Choose the site
buildSteps.detail: The machine needs cheap, abundant electricity and a wide safety zone. A lunar track would sit in vacuum and use solar arrays or a small reactor.

buildSteps.title: Build the accelerator
buildSteps.detail: A centrifuge is a large arm inside a circular vacuum chamber; an electromagnetic version is a long track of powered coils.

buildSteps.title: Install the power system
buildSteps.detail: Capacitors or flywheels store the energy for a launch and deliver it in a fraction of a second.

buildSteps.title: Integrate the payload
buildSteps.detail: The payload is hardened against thousands of g and bolted into an aerodynamic carrier with its own small motor.

buildSteps.title: Pump down and spin up
buildSteps.detail: Air is removed from the chamber and the arm is brought up to speed — or the coils are pulsed in sequence.

buildSteps.title: Release
buildSteps.detail: The carrier exits through a sealed port at the intended angle and speed; from Earth this is several times the speed of sound at low altitude.

buildSteps.title: Kick stage
buildSteps.detail: The small onboard rocket fires to raise the low release point into a stable orbit, since the machine alone cannot reach orbital velocity.

buildSteps.title: Recover or discard
buildSteps.detail: On Earth the carrier may parachute back for reuse; a lunar launcher would fire payload canisters that are caught or consumed in orbit.

prerequisites.why: some components can be ruggedised, but delicate satellites and humans cannot.
capacitor banks and flywheels exist, but not yet packaged for routine launch duty.
a ground launcher releases below orbital velocity, so a rocket must finish the job.

prerequisites.tech: Thermal protection for low-altitude hypersonic flight
prerequisites.why: re-entry shields work at high altitude; dense air at launch speed is a harsher case.
a lunar mass driver would need a large power source and automated building at a base.

pathway.milestone: suborbital test shots from a centrifugal accelerator, such as those flown by SpinLaunch
pathway.unlocks: data on release, aerodynamics and payload survival.

pathway.milestone: an orbital demonstration using a machine plus a kick stage
pathway.unlocks: proof that the concept can reach orbit, even with small payloads.

pathway.milestone: regular launch of rugged small payloads or bulk materials
pathway.unlocks: a niche alternative to rockets for fuel, water or raw materials.

pathway.milestone: a lunar electromagnetic launcher powered by surface solar or nuclear power
pathway.unlocks: exporting lunar material to orbit without burning propellant.
